fact: CHU Sahloul's communique says it had unified 180,000 health identifiers under the Identifiant unique de santé by 6 October 2026, the lead among public hospitals in the roll-out, and describes the identifier as linking each patient's health data and giving health structures access to the information whatever the place of care.

Ministry adviser Ines Ayadi says the national health identifier (EVAX identifier) is linked to the national ID card, social security number and school and university identifiers, and that medical files of about 100,000 people have been updated and linked to it, in public hospitals.

Mongi Slim hospital in La Marsa has piloted the national births-declaration platform since June 2026, declaring 202 births and assigning each a health identifier, with the platform meant to link to civil registry and social affairs systems and to wards and other health institutions.

fact: The Ministry of Health communique of 21 July 2026 says the Identifiant National de Sante, a unique personal health code, is being generalised progressively across all public health structures and university hospitals, after a pilot in reference hospitals that the ministry calls fully successful.

The ministry says the Sahetna.tn national citizen health platform is in final technical configuration, with a unified shared medical record to move clinical data between emergency departments and operating theatres.

The Kebili regional health director said on 16 July 2026 that the region's health institutions began adopting the national health identifier (INS), which unifies each patient's health file and links it to the national identity.
The regional director said the INS programme provides a fast, secure exchange of health data between the various medical institutions, under the ministry's digital transformation programmes.

The Tunisian Monitor reports, citing the Tunis Regional Directorate of Health, that over 9,000 patients were enrolled in the first weeks of the National Health Identifier, a lifetime code meant to connect a patient's medical history across providers, piloted from early July 2026 at Habib Thameur University Hospital using the national identity card.
Health authorities set out a phased plan to extend the NHI to all medical facilities nationwide by the end of 2026.

The Assembly approved on 12 February 2026 an amendment to the 2019 French Development Agency loan of 27.3 million euros for the E-Sante programme, which covers modernising hospital information systems in 24 university hospitals; about 16% was drawn and the minister cited stronger interconnection between hospitals.
